punchline: Soros built a method on the premise that he would sometimes be wrong.
thirty_sec: George Soros chose Karl Popper as his LSE tutor and built an approach on fallibility: he says he expects to be wrong some of the time, takes the loss when proven wrong, and may increase the bet when right; Black Wednesday 1992 is the famous trade.
question: What would have to happen for you to admit your current plan is wrong, and is it written down?
key_contrast: A stated exit rule, not confidence alone.
